_what_this_is: The ONE enumerated list of reviewer-owned pack documents, by EXACT name. Round 28, the challenger's B-10 (P1): manifest-digests.py enumerated them here while test/tool-commands-are-isolated.test.ts described the same set with a name PATTERN, so a document could be reviewer-owned in one instrument and author-owned in the other — and a pattern silently exempts the next file that happens to match it, which is round 23's F-42 reintroduced at the same width. Both instruments now read THIS file. A name is added here when a reviewer announces a report; no pattern, no inference, and a reviewer-looking file that is absent is a PROBLEM rather than an exemption.
_reviewer_reports_is_a_MAP_since_round_5: ROUND 50, the challenger's R48-F3 (P1): an enrolment line here is a one-file, routine-looking edit that exempted a document from the law entirely (303 passed with a plant enrolled), so it was CAMOUFLAGED and not licensed. Three teeth now. (1) This is a MAP from EXACT NAME to sha256, and both instruments refuse unless every key matches 'looks_like_reviewer' and every value is 64 hex characters — enrolling an author-owned document, or a name that is not reviewer-shaped, is refused BY NAME instead of exempting it. (2) The bytes are verified against the recorded digest wherever the pack is present, which also closes the one case the seal's name-set net was the only net for: an enrolled file whose BYTES change between the passes. (3) This file is pinned in tools/law-bytes.json, so any enrolment changes a digest there too and is refused unless that pin moves in the SAME commit. DECLARED LIMIT: a plant RENAMED into reviewer shape and enrolled WITH its true digest, with the law-bytes pin updated in the same commit, passes — that is the two-file limit, and in the diff it is a new reviewer name plus two new digests, which is what review reads.
_looks_like_reviewer_is_for_MESSAGES_and: ROUND 30, the challenger's F-53 (P2). This pattern must NEVER decide an exemption — that is B-10, and `reviewer_reports` above is the only thing that exempts. It decides WORDING: a file whose name has this shape but is absent from the list is an UNENUMERATED reviewer report, not an author-owned document, and telling the author to edit it routes them to the one repair the pack forbids for a reviewer's frozen bytes. Both instruments read this one pattern so the two messages cannot drift apart.
_looks_like_reviewer_restriction: F-54, round 32: this pattern is TEXT compiled by two engines. Python's end anchor also matches before a final newline and JS's does not, so the Python side must read it with fullmatch semantics and the JS side with ^...$ and no m flag. Use only constructs both engines read identically: no \\Z, no lookbehind, no named groups, no inline flags. A cross-engine arm in test/tool-commands-are-isolated.test.ts reds if the two verdicts differ on the same name. ROUND 53: the suffix group widened from `(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?` to `(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)*` because a reviewer froze `P5-CHALLENGE-2a4d105-ADDENDUM-01.md`, whose name carries TWO suffix segments, and the single-segment pattern did not route it: the pack arm counted it as author-owned and refused REFUSED-PACK-NOT-THE-PINNED-SET (a RED, not a silent pass, which is the shape this file is supposed to have). What the widening does and does not do: it only decides which names MAY be enrolled, never which are exempt — enrolment still requires the EXACT name here and the file's TRUE digest, verified against its bytes in both instruments — so the standing declared limit is unchanged, which is that an author-owned document named into reviewer shape AND enrolled with its true digest is outside both scans and bounded by review of the diff. Widening a SHAPE is a change to be read in that light: `-[A-Za-z0-9]+` segments only, both engines reading it identically, and the three reports frozen for this head enrolled in the same commit.
